author: barnabasbusa
content:
Here are the teku error logs, with the noise stripped out. Bottom line: all 14 teku nodes are still stuck at slot 49149, and the logs show the DA retriever failing on early Gloas blocks plus a corrupted RPC-abort path underneath it.

The load-bearing failure — DA never completes for Gloas blocks. Teku's custody retriever fails continuously on the first post-fork blob blocks (here slot 49176, block 0x0282dc78…):

DEBUG - SimpleSidecarRetriever.Request failed for DataColumnSlotAndIdentifier[slot=49176,
  blockRoot=0x0282dc78…d6d048, columnIndex=70] due to: DasColumnNotAvailableException

Its outbound data_column_sidecars_by_root requests fail two ways: peers answer response: <empty> (0 of the ~70–94 columns requested), or the request times out — RpcTimeoutException: Rpc request timed out after 10 sec: Timed out waiting for response chunk 0 (343 occurrences on teku-geth-1 alone in 40 min). Without the columns, the availability check never passes, imports stall, and the head stays at 49149. Notably, an inbound request at 08:04 shows teku itself serving 94 columns for a newer block (#49220) — so post-fork gossip decode works (the #9929 highest-milestone schema bug did self-heal at the fork as expected); it's specifically the req/resp backfill for the blocks it must import first that's dead.

Secondary teku bugs on the request-abort path (worth reporting upstream — this is teku-internal corruption, not network weather):
```
ERROR - Encountered error while processing response
java.util.ConcurrentModificationException
  at java.util.ArrayList.forEach
  at ...snappy.SnappyFramedCompressor$SnappyFramedDecompressor.close
  at ...LengthPrefixedPayloadDecoder.close(LengthPrefixedPayloadDecoder.java:134)
  at ...RpcResponseDecoder.close(RpcResponseDecoder.java:143)
  at ...Eth2OutgoingRequestHandler.abortRequest(Eth2OutgoingRequestHandler.java:242)

```

author: barnabasbusa
content:
with companions IllegalStateException: Trying to reuse disposed decoder instance (13x) and io.netty.util.IllegalReferenceCountException: refCnt: 0 (37x). When a column request times out and gets aborted, the decoder is closed from one thread while another is still feeding it — under the post-fork timeout storm this fires constantly.

General p2p distress (symptom, not cause): 550x StreamTimeoutException on ping, 175x on goodbye, 524x Connection reset, 403x PeerDisconnectedException, 50x DroppedRpcPartsException: Queued low priority RPC parts were dropped — teku is churning through peers, which is partly self-inflicted (half its peer set is wedged lighthouse/prysm nodes) and partly the abort-path corruption killing connections.

The one WARN flooding the fleet otherwise is just Validator *** Skipped aggregation … nothing to aggregate — a downstream consequence of not following the head, not a lead. Also seen once per node at 07:44: Failed to publish proposer preferences for epoch 1536, the first Gloas-duty failure pre-fork.

The open question for the teku team is why every peer returns empty for by_root column requests on early Gloas blocks while the chain's active clients (lodestar/nimbus/grandine) clearly hold that data — that could be a request-encoding/digest mismatch on teku's side or a serving gap on theirs.
